newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore OTCs slip on talk of cut in settlement.
newsitem.headline: Singapore OTCs slip on talk of cut in settlement.

text.p: Malaysian over-the-counter (OTC) stocks, which saw heavy buying throughout most of Wednesday, slipped in late afternoon on speculation of a cut in the stock settlement period, dealers said.
They said talk there would be an announcement soon that the stock settlement period would be cut to three days from five days currently, caused some panic selling in the last hour.
"I think this will be a temporary dampener on OTC stocks, an excuse for syndicates to take profit," said one remisier.
The UOB OTC index lost 4.97 points to 1,354.45, off its high of 1,373.44.
"If there is such an announcement, it must state from which date of purchasing it affects, otherwise there will be a lot of confusion," a dealer said.

Foreign tranches of blue chips saw a bit more selling after Morgan Stanley Capital International said it was cutting the weighting of some companies in its index. OCBC foreign and SIA foreign fell by Singapore S$0.40 and S$0.20 respectively.
The Straits Times Industrials Index rose 14.10 points to 2,216.07. Total volume was 596 million shares with losers ahead of gainers by 264 to 148. REUTER
